articles.title: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Gameplay Reveal Gives Extended Look at Combat, Exploration, and Traversal
articles.summary: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons recently released its long-awaited gameplay reveal at gamescom, and it gave us an extended look at main character Kaatri and the powers she has at her disposal.
body: If you weren’t already aware, Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons is a single-player, third-person, open-world action-adventure game from developer Invoke Studios where you wield forbidden magic to bend the rules, outwit obstacles, and overcome challenges through creativity. Kaatri is the warlock, and the gameplay reveal begins with her and Tasha, her witch queen patron. We see Tasha upgrade Kaatri’s Warlock’s Eye, which allows her to see Raw Magic and is the key to finding new spells and improving the ones she has.

From there, Kaatri moves to Darkon, a Domain of Dread pulled directly from D&D. It’s unstable and on the verge of being ripped apart by Mists. There is time to explore Darkon, but it’s filled with danger and opportunity around every corner.

Exploration is clearly a big focus of Warlock. As you travel through Darkon, you’ll need to stay alert and use magic to help you make your way. Your Warlock’s Eye will point you toward Raw Magic, but it’ll be up to you to figure out what to do with it. You need to pay attention to the sights and sounds around you and decide what deserves your attention.
points: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons recently released its long-awaited gameplay reveal at gamescom, and it gave us an extended look at main character Kaatri and the powers she has at her disposal.

articles.title: GTA 6's Relationship Mechanic Is 'Cheating' on Your Real-Life Partner and Break Up Worthy, According to Angry Spouses
articles.summary: A bunch of angry spouses on social media believe that Grand Theft Auto 6's in-depth relationship mechanic is equivalent to cheating on your real life partner and worth breaking up over.
body: A swath of angry spouses on social media believe that Grand Theft Auto 6's in-depth relationship mechanic is equivalent to cheating on your real-life partner and worth breaking up over.

Last week, we got a boatload of details on Grand Theft Auto 6 thanks to media previews and an extended look at the game from Rockstar itself. One of the big takeaways from this media blitz is that there is an actual relationship between the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, that players can nurture. You can take the other character on dates, do crimes together, text them, and even hold hands (aw!). For some people, though, that last detail causing tensions in their real life relationships.
Over on TikTok, a variety of concerned partners stated that wouldn't allow their partner to play the game, and a concerning amount of comments on these posts echoed this sentiment.
points: A bunch of angry spouses on social media believe that Grand Theft Auto 6's in-depth relationship mechanic is equivalent to cheating on your real life partner and worth breaking up over.

articles.title: PS5 Adds Free Live And On-Demand Movie And TV Channels, In Exchange For Watching Ads
articles.summary: Out of nowhere, Sony has announced that free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) is now on PlayStation 5, allowing people to watch movies and TV shows for free, in exchange for watching ads.
body: FAST programming is growing in popularity, and some of the current market leaders include Roku, Tubi, and Pluto, among others. FAST content was already on PS5 through dedicated apps for some of those services, but now Sony is launching its own FAST channel. For its part, Microsoft offers some FAST channels apps like Tubi and Pluto on Xbox as well.

Available on PS5 in the US, the new "Live TV on PS5" comes from Sony's own Sony Pictures Television. There are more than 100 live channels, as well as on-demand programming spanning news, sports, movies, TV shows, and anime.

Some of the content available includes movies from MovieSphere, 50 Cent Action, FilmRise Free Movies, Sony One Horror Hits, and Cinevault. Some of the TV shows people can watch include The Walking Dead, Community, Unsolved Mysteries, and Hell's Kitchen. Anime programming available on the service includes Naruto, Sailor Moon, and Death Note, as well as some Crunchyroll channels. For sports fans, programming from Fox Sports, Nascar, NBC Sports Now, and UFC are available. There are also news and weather channels, along with "creator" content like Hot Ones and The Ringer programming.
points: Out of nowhere, Sony has announced that free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) is now on PlayStation 5, allowing people to watch movies and TV shows for free, in exchange for watching ads.
FAST content was already on PS5 through dedicated apps for some of those services, but now Sony is launching its own FAST channel.

articles.title: Shailene Woodley Reflects on Cut Mary Jane Role in The Amazing Spider-Man 2
articles.summary: You may recall that Shailene Woodley was cast as Mary Jane Watson in The Amazing Spider-Man 2. The Divergent and Big Little Lies actor shot her scenes opposite Andrew Garfield’s wall-crawler for what she now calls her “dream” role in the Marvel-Sony sequel, only to later find out she had been cut…
body: In a recent chat with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation’s Conversations (via The Hollywood Reporter ), Woodley recalled her disappointment when she learned a year after she’d shot her scenes that she had been cut from Amazing Spider-Man 2.

“I was cast as Mary Jane for Spider-Man, which was my dream. Oh my god, Spider-Man’s my favorite superhero; Mary Jane was my favorite character growing up. So, when I got it, I was like, ‘This is so exciting!'” Woodley said.
The Amazing Spider-Man 2 ends with the death of Emma Stone’s Gwen Stacy, and the filmmakers said at the time that was one reason they cut Woodley’s Mary Jane from the movie.

“Shailene is a brilliant actress, and she did a great couple days of work,” director Marc Webb said. “But it was very difficult to introduce someone as a competing love interest when so much is on the table with Peter and Gwen.”

articles.title: Mortal Shell 2 Update Fixes The Game’s Stingy Economy
articles.summary: Developer Cold Symmetry continues to tinker with Mortal Shell 2, recently dropping a massive update that makes some substantial changes to its latest souls-like action-RPG.
body: Released on August 29, Mortal Shell 2's Week 1 Update makes some of the game's heaviest weapons stronger to compensate for their slowness. For example, the Obsidian Hammer hits way harder, and The Great Martyr's Blade had its damage output increased to make up for this change missing in the last patch. Overall, Cold Symmetry said that heavier weapons deal way more damage and poise now.

The headlining feature, though, is the overhaul to the economy. Before this patch, Glimpses (a currency used to upgrade your shells ) and Tarcores (a currency used to upgrade your Tarstones ) were incredibly limited in the world. With this new patch, however, both currencies are much more plentiful in the game.

To start, Tarcores are easier to collect now through a new set of items known as Fragile Tarstones. These pieces of equipment break after their durability depletes and, once broken, they yield Tarcores so you can upgrade your favorite Tarstones to their max levels more reliably.
points: Developer Cold Symmetry continues to tinker with Mortal Shell 2, recently dropping a massive update that makes some substantial changes to its latest souls-like action-RPG.

articles.title: Xbox CEO Reacts To The Irony Of Rising Console Prices Being An Issue That Microsoft Itself Contributed To
articles.summary: The price of an Xbox console today is higher than ever, and it was Microsoft's own massive push into the AI space that led to this, at least in part. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has now reacted to this ironic development, saying in an interview that she thinks it's great that GPUs are being used for…
body: "Gaming has always been a proving ground for the GPU. I think it is wonderful that there are more uses for this technology around the world," she told the BBC. "AI is fundamentally changing a lot of things. So our job as Xbox, as we continue on our next generation, is to take into consideration what's happening in the world and build the best experience for our players."

Following multiple rounds of price increases, the cheapest new Xbox--the Xbox Series S--now sells for $500, which is $200 more than what it cost at launch in 2020. Sharma said that for the next generation of consoles, including Microsoft's Helix platform, the company will need to think more about "efficiency and affordability, alongside performance."

Sharma also stated that Helix may not be a single device but rather a group of systems. "We've been hard at work on a great next generation, a great family of devices for Helix, and we'll share more soon," she said.
points: The price of an Xbox console today is higher than ever, and it was Microsoft's own massive push into the AI space that led to this, at least in part.

articles.title: All Adventure Effects and what they do in Pokémon Go
articles.summary: Adventure Effects are unique buffs that some legendary Pokémon can offer in Pokémon Go. These effects usually cost Stardust and some candy to activate, but will provide some kind of perk in or out of battle for a set amount of time.
body: So far, Adventure Effects are limited to special types of legendary Pokémon — usually ones with unique forms. (Though... Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon really got shafted by being released before Adventure Effects were a thing, huh?) These also usually debut during a big event, like a yearly Go Fest, making them somewhat rare and valuable.
Below we list the various Adventure Effects in Pokémon Go, alongside what they do, and what you need to do to unlock them.

Some Adventure Effects require you to have a specific form, whereas some others may require the Pokémon to know a specific move. Some effects even require both of those things, so make sure you're looking at what moves your Pokémon knows before you fuse them or change their forms, if you want their Adventure Effect.
You can also spend more Stardust, Mega Energy, and/or candy to extend the duration of the effects. Only one can be active at a time, though.

articles.title: “Aggressively” Selling PS5s Isn’t Needed, As Sony Focuses On Making More From Existing Owners
articles.summary: This November will mark the sixth anniversary of the PlayStation 5 console's launch, but in the years since its arrival, the gaming market has changed dramatically. The trend of consoles becoming cheaper over time has vanished this generation, as the PS5 now costs more today than it did in 2020…
body: "We are in the latter half of the lifetime cycle of a PS console," Totoki said to the Wall Street Journal. "That means that we do not need to aggressively sell the console today. And rather than that, we're focusing on recurring revenue from the current user base. And already, PS Plus has more than 125 million MAU (monthly active users) today. And how to monetize from the users is quite important for us."

Totoki wasn't clear by what he meant exactly in terms of aggressive PS5 sales, although it likely comes down to Sony not needing to discount the console or even sell it at a loss to draw in new users.

At the same time, Sony is preparing to move toward an all-digital future, as over 80% of games purchased for the console are done so through its digital storefront. Once Sony begins to phase out game discs starting January 2028, plugging that gap should result in a sizable jump in its profits.

PS5 lifetime sales have reached 95.3 million units sold as of July 31, 2026. At the same time, the company is starting to feel the pressure from rising prices. Compared with the same period in 2025, console sales declined by 36% in the last quarter.

articles.title: Naughty Dog Confirms Major Intergalactic Milestone Ahead of Sony's State of Play
articles.summary: The Last of Us and Uncharted developer Naughty Dog is hard at work on its next game, the sci-fi space adventure Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and has just hit a major milestone in the PlayStation 5 exclusive's development.
body: In a post on Bluesky, Naughty Dog announced: "That is a wrap on the very ambitious Intergalactic cinematic shoot! This cast killed it! Cannot wait to show you their incredible work when the time is right!"

The post features a picture of Intergalactic star Tati Gabrielle wearing a performance capture suit and wielding a prop gun, but doesn't reveal much beyond that. Fortunately, we can look back at Naughty Dog's precedent to infer what wrapping on a game's cinematic shoot means for its release date.

Back in April 2019, Neil Druckmann, game director of The Last of Us Part 2, announced that performance capture shooting had wrapped "on Ellie, Joel, and the most ambitious cinematic shoot we’ve ever done." The Last of Us Part 2 ultimately shipped in June 2020, after a pair of delays. The Last of Us Part 2 was originally slated for release on Feb. 21, 2020, but Druckmann said the game was delayed because “we simply didn’t have enough time to bring the entire game up to a level of polish we would call Naughty Dog quality.”

articles.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Reviews Say Capcom Has a Fourth Hit on Its Hands this Year
articles.summary: If you thought Capcom's blistering hot streak in 2026 was bound to end, you might be right. But it's not ending with Onimusha: Way of the Sword. The samurai action game revives Capcom's long-dormant series after 20 years (discounting remasters), and it bucks a big trend from the last five years.
body: Capcom's fresh take on action combat has gone over quite well with reviewers. At the time of writing, Onimusha: Way of the Sword 's Metacritic score is sitting at 86 — three points lower than Resident Evil Requiem 's 89, one point higher than Pragmata, which settled at 85, and on par with Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection. Whether that's enough to give Onimusha: Way of the Sword a shot at showing up at The Game Awards 2026 for more categories in addition to best action game, well, that's another story.

Most reviews, even the generally positive ones, balance high praise for Way of the Sword 's combat and storytelling with consistent criticism of how much extra stuff Capcom included in the game. Polygon's Giovanni Colantonio called it a "battle worth surviving," despite how sorely it tested his patience at times.

"Even when your power is rising through piecemeal RPG progression, it always feels like you’re in the duel of your life," he wrote. "And as old foes you swear you vanquished already rear their ugly heads again, you have no choice but to give up or stand and fight."
points: If you thought Capcom's blistering hot streak in 2026 was bound to end, you might be right.
But it's not ending with Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
The samurai action game revives Capcom's long-dormant series after 20 years (discounting remasters), and it bucks a big trend from the last five years.

articles.title: Cult simulator Join Us recruits four real ex-cult members to "experience the game's darkly satirical take on cult life"
articles.summary: Join Us, the upcoming co-op game where you can establish your own cult, has recruited four former cult members to "recruit followers, build their compounds, define their beliefs, and experience the game's darkly satirical take on cult life".
body: While developer Wolf Haus was cautious enough to bleep out the actual cult names, they did talk a little about their time with their respective cults, with Ariel talking about his former belief that there was a UFO coming to take him "home" on 12th May 2001, and Javier reflecting on his days in a "holistic rejuvenation centre" where they grew all of their own food.

It's an extraordinary experiment, not least because, as Wolf Haus itself admits, the reactions were "mixed", with one very excited about growing their own tomatoes, and another confidently declaring "no one's going to like this".

Join Us is an open-world survival game where you can build your own cult, recruit followers, survive the apocalypse, and play solo or in co-op with up to four players. It's currently slated to release in March 2027 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Officially the Bloodiest GTA Game Yet
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 aims to be a more grounded, realistic experience than the rest of the franchise. The game still has a sense of humor, but the overall vibe is much more serious. One of the major things contributing to that tone shift is the way GTA 6 handles violence.
body: GTA 6 's heightened violence was visible throughout Netflix's Extended Look, which debuted Aug. 27. During an early shootout, the game slowed down and zoomed in on an enemy who is shot in the face by Jason, one of the game's protagonists. The shotgun shrapnel can be seen shearing away fleshy chunks of the man's face.

Later on, Lucia is slammed against a wall by a large man. The impact of her skull against the wall leaves a blood spatter. The sense of danger heightens as Lucia tries to crawl away, only to be forcefully held down by the assailant. Lucia ends the encounter by stabbing the man in the eye with one of her heels. The moment is played for laughs — Lucia tells the man that wearing heels is just as painful — but the game's graphical fidelity makes the gory segment feel unusually brutal.

articles.title: Sony's next PlayStation State of Play coming this Thursday, followed by a Japan and Asia-dedicated showcase
articles.summary: Our next port of call when it comes to major livestreams filled with game reveals isn't too far off. Sonytoday announced the date of the next PlayStation State of Play presentation. The showcase airs Thursday, 3rd September.
body: It will be streamed live in the afternoon in Europe, kicking off at 6am PT / 9am ET / 2pm BST / 3pm CEST. In a blog post, Sony said to expect "updates and announcements" from both PlayStation Studios as well as third-party developers. The show ends with an "extended look" at the world of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

Immediately following the show, another will begin: State of Play Japan. The second showcase, hosted by Japanese voice actor Yuki Kaji, will focus on games from Japan and Asia. Sony said to expect "new gameplay, announcements, and more". As always both shows will be accessible on PlayStation's YouTube and Twitch channels, though Sony didn't say how long either showcase is going to be.

The existence of this week's State of Play leaked just a few days ago, when reliable insider NateTheHate posted about it on X. It's not entirely surprising Sony would host a State of Play in September, of course; the company held one for the last several years, except this year's edition falls earlier in the month than the most recent two.

articles.title: Haunted Chocolatier's development has been 'very productive' in recent months, Eric Barone says: 'Working on Haunted Chocolatier is what I’m most eager and driven to do'
articles.summary: We find ourselves at the end of another month, and as ever, the passing phases of the moon leave us asking the same question: What's going on with Haunted Chocolatier?
body: Knowing all too well how the hungry masses clamor for details about his next game, Stardew Valley developer Eric "ConcernedApe" Barone has posted another of his intermittent check-in blogs to confirm that, yes, he's still hard at work on Haunted Chocolatier. And while he's still not sharing many specifics, Barone sounds like he's satisfied with his recent progress.

"I'm still here, still making progress. Thanks for waiting and sorry it’s taking so long," Barone wrote. "I’ve been very productive on this project lately even though I am busy with many things. Working on Haunted Chocolatier is what I’m most eager and driven to do, out of everything."

While he acknowledged the years that have already gone into Haunted Chocolatier's development—he first announced the game in 2021—Barone said he doesn't "stress too much about how long it’s taking." The ongoing success of Stardew Valley affords him the ability to prioritize his own criteria for quality over meeting any arbitrary deadline. As he's said in previous development check-ins, he's unwilling to release anything he's not entirely satisfied with.

videos.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Review
videos.summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker reviewed by Travis Northup on PlayStation 5, also available on PC and Xbox Series X/S.
body: "The Blood of Dawnwalker is my new favorite vampire game and one of the best story-driven RPGs I’ve played in a long time. The day/night cycle that has you juggling human and vampiric forms is awesome, and the constraints placed on how you spend your limited time ends up being one of the coolest, most wonderfully stressful parts of the adventure. Combat has a bit of a learning curve to it, but gets under your skin in all the right ways once you get the hang of it. Combine that with a story filled with memorable characters, gut wrenching decisions, and more endings than I’m ever likely to see, and this adventure kept me firmly in its thrall. Even if you aren’t particularly into the vampire fantasy, this is one that any RPG fan should absolutely not miss."
points: The Blood of Dawnwalker reviewed by Travis Northup on PlayStation 5, also available on PC and Xbox Series X/S.

videos.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Review
videos.summary: Onimusha: Way of the Sword reviewed by Will Borger on PS5, also available on Xbox Series X, PlayStation 5, and Switch 2.
body: "It’s a testament to Onimusha: Way of the Sword’s combat that I could beat it without using some of the systems designed to help you progress – not because you don’t need them, but because it leaves room for you to truly understand its action and overcome their absence through sheer determination. Even if I hadn’t intentionally made things harder for myself, though, I still would have loved spending time with the charismatic denizens of this world, all of whom are as well acted as they are animated. I still would have thought that Musashi himself was one of the coolest, most interesting protagonists in any video game, and I would have loved going on this journey with him. I still would have savored the creative fights against dozens of impressive bosses. My journey reflected Musashi's, and Onimusha made that possible. The best part of life is the challenge. You have to learn to love the fight."

videos.title: Introducing Live TV on PS5
videos.summary: Starting later today, Live TV on PS5® by Sony Pictures will be available to PS5® players in the U.S., bringing more than 100 live channels and a growing selection of on-demand entertainment directly to the Media section of PS5®.
body: Discover movies, TV shows, anime, sports, news, creator-led programming and more — free with ads and no subscription required.
To get started, head to the Media tab on your PS5® console and select Live TV on PS5®.
Programming availability may vary by local TV markets and may change over time.
